clue.text: Legally seize goods the underworld transport

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the name stands for the underworld itself
a train is a means of transport

explanation.surface: Gangsters' transport is impounded by bailiffs acting under the law.
explanation.definitionFit: To distrain is the legal term for confiscating property to force payment of a debt.

clue.text: Condescend to include second scheme

indicators.note: one word is made to include another, so the second sits inside the first

parts.note: to condescend is to deign

explanation.surface: Someone deigns to add a second item to a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A design is a plan or plot, the same as a scheme.

clue.text: Getting learners to reverse is a mistake

indicators.note: the clue asks the word for learners to be turned round and read backwards

parts.note: pupils are learners at school

explanation.surface: Learner drivers are told that reversing badly is an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is a small error or blunder.

clue.text: Concerned with assistance for the provinces

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading
alms are charitable help given to the poor

explanation.surface: Someone is busy arranging aid for the regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Realms are kingdoms or domains, territories like provinces.

clue.text: The British TT?

parts.note: the TT is a motorcycle race held on the Isle of Man, so it is a race on an island; the British, living on islands, are also called a people of that kind

explanation.surface: A question about the famous Tourist Trophy motorcycle race.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is a motorcycle race on the Isle of Man; the phrase also names the British people, an islander nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Island race is a traditional phrase for the British people, and the TT is literally a contest held on an island.

clue.text: The way men ran new organisation

indicators.note: the letters of the words men and ran are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Men ran a newly formed group in a particular style.
explanation.definitionFit: A manner is a mode or method of doing something.

clue.text: Barter -an irregular arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters of barter and an into a new order

explanation.surface: A trading deal made in an unusual way.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrant describes something deviating from the normal course, so unusual or abnormal.

clue.text: Mean with a supporter usually

parts.note: the mean or average is the norm
an ally is a supporter

explanation.surface: An average person with a backer, as is common.
explanation.definitionFit: Normally means as a rule, in the ordinary way.

clue.text: Residing when infirm where there's a good view

indicators.note: infirm means weak or unsteady, so the letters of residing are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Living somewhere when frail, with a nice outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringside seats beside a boxing ring give spectators the closest look at the action.

clue.text: May well be smartly dressed when it's appropriate

explanation.surface: A smart outfit is fitting for the occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the answer as two words: able to wear a suit, so likely to be smartly dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitable means fitting or right for the purpose; read as suit plus able it means capable of being formally dressed.

clue.text: Oppress a beast with no backing

parts.note: a bear is a large wild animal

indicators.note: the word no is backed up, read from right to left

explanation.surface: Persecuting an animal without support.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear on is to weigh down on or press heavily upon, as oppression does.

clue.text: A fellow into fruit, being a lover of good food

indicators.note: the fellow goes into the fruit, sitting inside its letters

parts.note: a gourd is a fleshy fruit of the squash family
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A man inside a fruit, being a food enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmand is someone who loves eating, a glutton or connoisseur of fine dishes.

clue.text: Fears sadder outcome

indicators.note: the outcome of reworking sadder is a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Worries about a gloomier result.
explanation.definitionFit: To dread something is to fear it greatly.

clue.text: Cleans up -assume it's the lottery

parts.note: sweeps means cleans up with a broom
to take something on is to assume it

explanation.surface: Someone who wins everything takes it as luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweepstake is a draw in which all stakes go to the winners, a form of lottery.

clue.text: A person gaining stature as 25's assistant?

explanation.surface: A teenager shooting up helps the worker in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the phrase as 'grow-in lad', a youngster who helps someone grow plants, the worker of 25-across.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy still getting taller is a youth getting bigger; one who grows plants would have such a helper.

clue.text: Making light of taking the fare

explanation.surface: Mocking someone while eating the food.
explanation.walkthrough: Fare here is food, not a ticket price.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to mock or jeer, and also, informally, to eat greedily.

clue.text: This creature dug in near-frenzy

annotationWithheld.why: This creature dug in near-frenzy (3-5): ATE for 'dug in' plus an anagram of NEAR leaves a T unaccounted for; no parse gives all eight letters and a search of the exact text found nothing

clue.text: Claim X has been taken in by dreadful creep

indicators.note: the ten goes inside the reworked letters of creep
dreadful signals that the letters of creep are mangled

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Ten was conned by an awful sneak making a false claim.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretence is a claim, often false, as in a pretence to learning.

clue.text: Drawn together, gave a pledge

explanation.surface: Pulled together, someone made a promise.
explanation.definitionFit: Contracted means shrunk or tightened, and also bound oneself by agreement.

clue.text: Whine about divine pool

indicators.note: the whine goes about the divine, wrapped around it

parts.note: to pule is to whimper or whine
DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a clergyman or divine

explanation.surface: Complaints about a holy spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A puddle is a small pool of water.

clue.text: Get around a girl or get the bird

indicators.note: the word get goes around the girl's name

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Pursuing a girl or being jeered at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get the bird' is an idiom for being booed, which disguises the plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The gannet is a large seabird.

clue.text: Alarm caused by misdoing after the start of term

indicators.note: the misdoing is placed after that letter
the start of the word term is its opening letter

parts.note: an error is a wrongdoing or mistake

explanation.surface: A school panic caused by bad behaviour early in the term.
explanation.definitionFit: Terror is extreme fear, the same as alarm.

clue.text: Quick point made by craft

parts.note: fleet means swift
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A rapid point made by cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleets are groups of ships, so many sea craft.

clue.text: Kiss big copper — and none too soon!

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, meaning big
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
something late arrives none too soon

explanation.surface: A large policeman gets a kiss, and it is overdue.
explanation.definitionFit: To osculate is a formal or humorous word meaning to kiss.

clue.text: Speak of popular heavyweight, English

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: Talking about a well-liked English boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: To intone is to utter or recite, especially in a level chanting voice.

clue.text: A worker in bed

parts.note: seems to describe someone toiling under the covers, but the bed is a flower bed

explanation.surface: Someone working while lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tends plants works in flower beds.

clue.text: Fish catch — could be a stone

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: A haul of fish might include a pebble.
explanation.definitionFit: Garnet is a deep red semi-precious gemstone.

clue.text: One who doesn't go for animals without a checkout

definitions.text: One who doesn't go for animals

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes animals and avoids a check.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer as de- (without) plus tester (one who checks things out), a punning reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who loathes things is a hater; a person with no examiner would be tester-less.
